notes.text: Kirill Marchenko is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 60:17 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 61:12 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Oliver Ekman-Larsson has taken his spot beside Troy Stecher.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 31% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 123:50 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Dillon Boucher was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Cole Smith and Ryan Greene.

stakes: The Maple Leafs go in eighth in the Atlantic with 18 points, the Blackhawks eighth in the Central with 12 points.

CHI.head: The Blackhawks start a half-step behind
CHI.body: Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately, but they will be without Marchenko, and Chicago has home-ice advantage. The Blackhawks’ best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

TOR.head: The Maple Leafs start a half-step ahead
TOR.body: Toronto has been out-chancing opponents lately, but they will be without Marchenko, and Chicago has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Blackhawks can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Maple Leafs are desperate for a win
paras: The Maple Leafs are on a six-game losing streak, and the Blackhawks (5-13-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Winnipeg on Saturday. Going in, the Leafs are last in the Atlantic (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last in the Central (tied for 30th).

The Maple Leafs have played better than their record (.409) says: their chances are worth about .475, mostly because they’re 3-8 in one-goal games. The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.300) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .381, and their goaltending has held them back.
In their six-game skid, the Maple Leafs have been outscored 23-9, including 15-8 at 5-on-5.

The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest) and don’t block many shots (31st). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so the Maple Leafs have the edge over them on the power play. Chicago has scored 2.30 goals a game, the fewest in the league, and allowed 4.10, the second most. The Blackhawks’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Auston Matthews (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for eighth in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind. The Blackhawks’ scoring runs through Connor Bedard (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 14 GP), who has seven points in his last five games. Roman Kantserov (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 20 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Sergei Bobrovsky (3-8-2 / .881 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to start for Toronto, and Spencer Knight (5-10-1 / .882 SV% in 16 GS) for Chicago.
